learning_outcomes.text: Students know the history, structure, and application of automation systems in industry, households, vehicle, and traffic technology.

They understand the fundamentals of digital technology in automation, including topologies of modern automation systems, control technology (programmable logic controllers, microprocessor technology), basics of sensor technology and actuator technology, concepts of control engineering, and basic controller types.
Additionally, students learn the abstract representation of mechatronic systems, the creation of transfer functions, and the system simulation of mechatronic systems with MATLAB-Simulink.

syllabus_topics: Structures and signals in automated processes
Fundamentals of digital technology (binary coding, AD conversion, pulse width modulation)
Structure and functionality of digital controls
Case study of a mechatronic system
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded for a passed module exam and successful participation in the exercises as a study achievement (SL). The weighting of the grade for the final grade is according to ECTS points.
